cases.expected: preloadJsonSchemas is invoked with an empty collection and no exception is thrown
cases.description: When the internal `schemas` map is empty, `preloadJsonSchema()` should call `preloadJsonSchemas` with an empty iterable. The method must complete normally without throwing any exception.

cases.expected: preloadJsonSchemas is invoked with a collection containing exactly the single added JsonSchema instance
cases.description: Add one `JsonSchema` object to the private `schemas` map, then call `preloadJsonSchema()`. The method should forward a collection that contains exactly that schema to `preloadJsonSchemas`.

cases.expected: preloadJsonSchemas is invoked with a collection containing all added JsonSchema instances in insertion order
cases.description: Populate the `schemas` map with several `JsonSchema` objects (e.g., three). After invoking `preloadJsonSchema()`, verify that `preloadJsonSchemas` receives a collection that includes all those schemas preserving the map's insertion order.

cases.expected: preloadJsonSchemas is invoked with a collection that contains a null element, leading to a NullPointerException inside `preloadJsonSchemas` (if it does not tolerate nulls)
cases.description: Insert a key with a `null` value into the `schemas` map. When `preloadJsonSchema()` is executed, it forwards the map values (including the null). The expected behavior is that the underlying `preloadJsonSchemas` method will throw a `NullPointerException` because a null schema cannot be pre‑loaded. The test asserts that the exception propagates.

group: Exception propagation from a schema during preload

cases.expected: preloadJsonSchemas propagates the RuntimeException thrown by the offending JsonSchema
cases.description: Insert a mock JsonSchema into the internal `schemas` map whose `preloadJsonSchema` implementation throws a RuntimeException. When `PropertiesValidator.preloadJsonSchema()` is invoked, the exception should bubble up unchanged, confirming that the method does not swallow unexpected errors from individual schemas.

group: Repeated invocation does not alter internal state

cases.expected: preloadJsonSchemas receives the same collection on each call and the internal `schemas` map remains unchanged after each invocation
cases.description: Populate the `schemas` map with two distinct JsonSchema instances. Call `preloadJsonSchema()` twice in succession. Verify that both calls forward identical collections (same size, same order) and that the internal map still contains the original two entries after the second call.

group: Order preservation with mixed insertion patterns

cases.expected: preloadJsonSchemas receives schemas in the exact insertion order, even after intermediate removals and re‑insertions
cases.description: Add three schemas A, B, C to the map in that order, then remove B and re‑add a new schema D under the same key as B. The final insertion order should be A, C, D. After invoking `preloadJsonSchema()`, assert that the collection passed to `preloadJsonSchemas` follows this order, demonstrating that the LinkedHashMap ordering semantics are respected.

cases.expected: preloadJsonSchemas throws a ValidationException (or StackOverflowError) due to circular reference, which propagates from preloadJsonSchema
cases.description: Create two mock JsonSchema objects where each references the other (e.g., schema1's `$ref` points to schema2 and vice‑versa). Insert both into the `schemas` map. When `preloadJsonSchema()` is called, the underlying preload logic will encounter a circular reference and raise an exception. The test verifies that this exception is not caught inside `preloadJsonSchema`.

group: Null collection handling after map mutation

cases.expected: preloadJsonSchemas receives a collection that reflects the map state at call time; subsequent mutations to the map do not affect the already‑passed collection
cases.description: Add a JsonSchema instance to the map, invoke `preloadJsonSchema()`, then immediately clear the map. Using a spy on `preloadJsonSchemas`, confirm that the collection received during the call still contains the original schema, proving that the method passes a snapshot rather than a live view.

Insert a mock JsonSchema whose preloadJsonSchema implementation mutates the validator's internal `schemas` map (e.g., adds a new entry) while `preloadJsonSchemas` is iterating over `schemas.values()`. When `PropertiesValidator.preloadJsonSchema()` is called, the concurrent modification should cause a `ConcurrentModificationException` which must propagate unchanged.

Add a mock JsonSchema to the validator where the schema's `preloadJsonSchema` method throws an `AssertionError`. Invoke `preloadJsonSchema()` and verify that the `AssertionError` is not caught by the method and bubbles up to the caller.

Using reflection, set the private `schemas` field of a `PropertiesValidator` instance to `null`. Call `preloadJsonSchema()` and expect a `NullPointerException` because the method attempts to invoke `values()` on a null map.
